breadcrumb: Channel letter signs: form, light and placement
h1: Channel letter signs: form, light and placement
lead: Channel letters use individually formed characters to create a strong business identity, often with illumination as part of the design. The visual result depends on letter shape, lighting direction, spacing and the building behind it. For a New York project, Vision Graphics can help organize the concept for technical review. Electrical supply, mounting conditions, property approval and service access all need to be resolved before a proposal becomes a production commitment. Begin with your artwork and a full view of the intended facade.

sections.html: Front-facing illumination emphasizes the letter faces, while a reverse-lit concept creates light behind the letters. The wall finish and distance from the surface can influence the appearance. Review a visual concept in both daytime and nighttime terms rather than judging only an isolated product rendering.

Confirm where the letters would mount, how wiring could be routed and who is responsible for electrical work, approvals and access. Existing power or a previous sign should not be assumed suitable. The final design requires product, mounting and site review before production is released.

items.p: Explore letter faces as the primary illuminated element.
Consider a halo effect against a suitable background surface.
Review how the mounting approach affects appearance and site requirements.

items.a_html: The answer depends on the logo, wall, surroundings and desired appearance. Compare the concept against the actual location.

items.q: Can letters connect to existing power?
items.a_html: A qualified electrical review must establish whether the existing supply and wiring are appropriate. Do not assume compatibility.
